active_paradigms.idea: Smooth surrogate optimization with annealed LogSumExEx soft-min via scipy.optimize.minimize
active_paradigms.description: Replace the non-smooth greedy coordinate descent with a proper gradient-based local optimizer on a smooth surrogate: r_soft = -temperature * logsumexp(-areas/temperature) / hull_area, where hull_area is also smoothed via a log-sum-exp over convex hull support directions (or held fixed once the hull vertex set stabilizes). Use scipy.optimize.minimize with method='SLSQP' or 'L-BFGS-B' on all 26 coordinates, starting from the current best configuration and from symmetric seeds. Anneal the temperature from ~1e-2 down to ~1e-5 over successive minimize calls, warm-starting each stage. Analytic or finite-difference gradients both work since only 26 variables exist. This escapes the axis-aligned step-size limitations of the current coordinate descent, which can only move along 8 fixed directions and plateaus on the ratio objective.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary): smooth optimization can find exact local optima of the true objective that greedy 8-direction coordinate descent cannot reach, pushing combined_score above 1.0.
active_paradigms.cautions: Soft-min temperature must be annealed carefully; too cold makes gradients vanish. Keep the hull area term smooth by using a fixed hull or log-sum-exp over hull edge contributions. Guard against degenerate hulls (area < 1e-9) with a large penalty.

active_paradigms.idea: Symmetry-restricted parametric families with exhaustive low-dimensional search
active_paradigms.description: Restrict the search to configurations with exact 3-fold rotational symmetry: 13 = 1 + 4*3, i.e., a center point plus 4 orbits of 3 points each, parameterized by only ~9 free parameters (4 radii, 4 angles, plus center offset). Exhaustively grid-search this low-dimensional parameter space (radii in [0.05, 1.0], angles in [0, 2pi/3)) at coarse resolution, then refine the top candidates with the existing local search but allowing symmetry-breaking perturbations. Also try 13 = 1 + 6 + 6 (center + two hexagon orbits, 13 free params), and 13 = 3 + 5 + 5 style nests. The massive dimensionality reduction (9-13 params vs 26) means a near-exhaustive coverage of the symmetric subspace is feasible within the 240s budget, potentially finding structured optima that random restarts miss. Keep the best-of-all-families result and compare against the unconstrained incumbent.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized: structured families concentrate search effort on geometrically balanced configurations where the min-triangle bottleneck is naturally large.
active_paradigms.cautions: The optimal 13-point configuration likely has NO perfect symmetry (13 is prime, and known good Heilbronn configs are often asymmetric), so always run the unconstrained refinement as a final polish and comparison. Ensure determinism with fixed seeds and fixed grid ordering.

active_paradigms.idea: Bottleneck-guided LP moves: maximize the minimum triangle via linear programming on active constraints
active_paradigms.description: Formulate each local improvement step as a linear program: given the current configuration, the area of triangle (i,j,k) is an affine function of any single moved point p_i (area = 0.5*|cross(p_j - p_i, p_k - p_i)|; for fixed j,k and small moves the sign of the cross product is stable, making it linear). Solve max t subject to: for every triangle containing point i, linearized_area >= t, plus a trust region ||p_i - p_i^0|| <= delta, using scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS). Iterate over points i (or move all points with a joint LP using sequential linearization of all 286 area constraints), shrinking the trust region as convergence approaches. This directly optimizes the true max-min objective (not a surrogate) with exact global steps within each trust region, unlike coordinate descent which only tests 8 directions per point per step size. Alternate with occasional hull-area reduction moves (pulling interior hull vertices inward) since the ratio also improves by shrinking the hull.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized: LP steps provably find the best single-point move within the trust region, eliminating direction/step-size discretization error entirely.
active_paradigms.cautions: The min-area constraint set may be empty for aggressive t; use bisection on t with feasibility checks. The hull area changes as points move, so re-linearize every few iterations and only accept steps that strictly improve the true ratio. Handle degenerate triangles (zero gradient) by dropping those constraints and relying on the true-objective check.
